content:
alice_support: FYI customer Acme reported intermittent 401/403 errors from their CI pipeline when calling our inference endpoint. They say it started after a key rotation last week. Error in their logs: "insufficient_scope" and "token expired". They attached a short trace.

mike_eng: Can you paste the exact curl they used (headers) and the x-request-id from our side if available? Also which token type are they using — service account token or long-lived API key?

alice_support: They sent this snippet (redacted):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference/text_generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <CI_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-redwood", "input":"hello"}'
```
They said response 403 body: `{"error":"insufficient_scope", "message":"token missing required scope: inference:invoke"}`
Their pipeline is GitHub Actions using a token they requested from us as a service account CI token last year.

mike_eng: That error strongly implies token exists but doesn't include inference:invoke scope. Two failure modes: token minted with limited scopes OR token was rotated/renewed with a different scope set. Also if token TTL expired we'd see "token expired". Can you pull the x-request-id? deploy-bot: recent deploy for runtime v2.3.1 at 2025-10-29T02:10Z.

alice_support: Customer gave one request id: req_0a1b2c3d. I queried logs: `auth_service` for req_0a1b2c3d shows `token_id=ci_98765 scope_set=[billing:read] ttl_exp=169... expired_or_missing` and a follow up auth check failing for `inference:invoke`.

sara_security: Quick checklist: 1) Are they using the old global API key vs service account? 2) Did we recently change default token scopes for CI tokens? 3) Any IAM policy change pushed last week? I rolled out a scoped-token guard on Oct 25 to reduce leftover privileges; maybe that's related.

mike_eng: I can repro locally by minting a CI token with only billing:read. Repro steps:
```
# create token (admin api) - example
POST https://console.redwood.ai/internal/tokens
{
  "type": "ci",
  "service_account": "acme-svc-01",
  "scopes": ["billing:read"],
  "ttl": "30d"
}
# then call inference:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference/text_generate
# response: 403 insufficient_scope
```
So behavior is expected.

alice_support: Customer insists they had inference access before — they say token was created in Jan 2024 and we didn't change anything on their side.

sara_security: Two possibilities: 1) Token was rotated via our support flow and new token got narrower scopes. 2) We tightened default CI token scopes during the Oct 25 rollout. Ops note: we changed default CI scopes to `billing:read` only unless request included explicit inference scope. Ticketing flow may not have requested inference:invoke for that account.

mike_eng: Proposed remediation steps for customer: A) Create a new CI token scoped only to `inference:invoke` (+ minimal others like `models:read` if needed). B) Recommend using short TTL (e.g., 7 days) and automated rotation from GH Actions. C) Store token in GitHub Secrets / Secret Manager. D) If possible switch to OIDC/GitHub Actions OIDC provider to mint ephemeral tokens.

alice_support: I've drafted guidance to send them. Also asked them to confirm whether their runner uses the old token in two places (build and integration test step) — common cause is one step updated, other still using old token.

mike_eng: For ops / internal steps if they want us to issue token we can do an admin token create: example request for our support script:
```
POST https://console.redwood.ai/support/create-ci-token
Auth: Support-Api-Key <redacted>
Body:
{
  "account_id":"acct_acme123",
  "service_account":"acme-svc-01",
  "scopes":["inference:invoke","models:read"],
  "ttl":"7d",
  "note":"Issued per support request 1751256789"
}
```
This will show up in audit logs and create token id `ci_abc123`.

sara_security: If we issue from support, add MFA/approval step for prod-scoped scopes. Also I want an entry in audit: query `auth_audit` for `account_id=acct_acme123` and timeframe last 90 days to show previous tokens and scope changes. Use internal quick query: `SELECT * FROM auth_audit WHERE account='acct_acme123' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50` or use web UI https://internal.redwood.ai/audit.

alice_support: I asked customer if they'd like us to issue a token. They replied: "Yes please, we can't update our app until EOD PST." I requested required scopes inference:invoke only.

mike_eng: I created token `ci_abc123` with TTL 7d and scopes [inference:invoke]. I also added a note and flagged the creation for sara_security for review.

sara_security: Reviewed and approved. Remind them to rotate monthly and prefer ephemeral OIDC where possible. Also recommended limiting permission to specific model(s) with `model:use:gpt-4-redwood` if available.

alice_support: Sent token to customer via their secure channel and gave these steps to update GH Actions:
```
- Add secret REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN in repo secrets
- In workflow: 
  - name: Call Redwood
    run: |
      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_CI_TOKEN }}" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        --data '{"model":"gpt-4-redwood","input":"hi"}' \
        https://api.redwood.ai/v1/inference/text_generate
```
Also included link to docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/ci-tokens for best practices.

alice_support: Customer confirmed pipeline green after swapping token. They said they found one lingering secret in an older repo that still had the rotated token and will rotate that too.

mike_eng: Useful followups for us: 1) Add a support checklist entry to ask if the token needs inference scope during token requests. 2) Consider a short notice on the Oct 25 rollout communicating default scope changes (if we haven't). 3) Build a small audit dashboard to show CI tokens missing common scopes.

sara_security: I'll send a quick change to the support runbook and add an automated check in the token-issuance UI to require a justification field when requesting inference scope.

alice_support: Closing once I confirm they rotated the older secret. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy v2.3.1 health-checks passed :white_check_mark:

alice_support: Confirmed customer rotated other secret and pipeline stayed green. Closing thread.
